source_direct_findings: GitHub routes a self-hosted job only to an online and idle runner matching the job's runs-on labels and groups; otherwise the job remains queued until a matching runner comes online.
If an assigned runner does not pick up the job within 60 seconds, GitHub re-queues the job, so queue state alone cannot identify one unique root cause.
Self-hosted runner labels are cumulative for eligibility: a runner must satisfy every requested label, and group constraints are additional when used.
On Linux systems using systemd, the GitHub Actions runner can be installed and managed as a boot-persistent service with the runner-provided svc.sh install/start/status/stop lifecycle.

GitHub documents runner service logs through journalctl, including listener startup, connection, listening-for-jobs, job execution and completion events; these are stronger operational liveness witnesses than queued-job metadata alone but still are not product-runtime evidence.
GitHub documents an Ubuntu/Debian needrestart interaction and provides a configuration that prevents needrestart from restarting the Actions runner service during a workflow job.
Replacing a runner can require labels to be re-assigned; therefore service liveness and routing eligibility are separate properties.

supported: A thin runner-service liveness prerequisite is technically supported for the Linux/X64 WP510 transport surface.
Runner service liveness, runner registration/online state, label/group eligibility, job assignment, step execution and target-runtime receipt must remain separate evidence stages.
For an Ubuntu target, needrestart-induced runner restarts are a concrete operational failure mode worth explicitly fencing if the target uses needrestart.
not_supported: svc.sh status PASS does not prove GitHub-side online/idle eligibility.
GitHub-side online eligibility does not prove a job executed.
A queued job does not prove an F2 semantic failure.
Runner/service evidence cannot mint WP510 target-runtime, GWT, GRID10, J-Space, effect, training or whole-system credit.

counterhypothesis: The current WP510 runner was intentionally ephemeral or manually launched and no durable systemd service is desired; in that case a service prerequisite would add operational coupling without improving the product. E2 must inspect the actual controller/target runner lifecycle before recommending any build change.
next_discriminator: E2 architecture mapping: inspect the current WP510 controller workflow and available runner-lifecycle evidence for whether service persistence is intended, whether online/label eligibility is observable, and whether an Ubuntu needrestart fence is actually applicable. Do not modify the target or dispatch a new run in E2.
